newsitem.title: USA: NationsBank sees early merger savings.
newsitem.headline: NationsBank sees early merger savings.

text.p: NationsBank Corp told analysts on Monday the projected savings from its $9.8 billion merger with Boatmen's Bancshares Inc would occur sooner than originally forecast.

"The merger is going faster than we originally expected, and as a result some of the benefits and expenses previously scheduled to be realized in 1998 are now expected to occur in 1997," spokeswoman Susan Carr said in a telephone conference call with reporters after the release of fourth-quarter earnings.
NationsBank originally made several projectons when the merger with Boatmen's was first announced on August 30.
Carr said savings during 1997 are now expected to reach $175 million, higher than the initial estimate of $140 million.

In August, NationsBank estimated 1997 cash earnings of $3.3 billion, but the company now expects to beat that target, Carr said. In August, reported earnings were estimated at $2.9 billion, but now NationsBank expects to "equal or exceed" that figure, she said.
Cash basis earnings are operating net income minus amortization of goodwill.
Carr said NationsBank's goal is to repurchase 56 million shares and to buy back as many as possible before the end of 1997.
The share repurchase target includes 37 million of the 98 million shares that were issued to complete the Boatmen's deal, and an additional 19 million shares.

Boatmen's shareholders overwhelmingly opted to choose stock rather than cash in the merger, with 96 percent of the Boatmen's shares being acquired for stock. NationsBank had a goal of 60 percent stock, and the planned repurchase of 37 million shares is aimed at achieving that ratio.

Carr cautioned that earnings per share during 1997 would depend on the timing and amount of shares that were repurchased. She said the stock buybacks would depend on factors such as market conditions and the price of the shares.

While the company will realize savings faster than originally expected, it will also incur higher transition costs, Carr said. She said the company doubled its initial estimate of transition costs to $100 million from $50 million.
She said amoritzation of goodwill, originally estimated at $245 million, is now projected to be $286 million.
The greater amount of amortization reflects a rise in the price of NationsBank shares since the announcement of the merger in August, Carr said.
Carr said NationsBank was confident it would exceed a goal of achieving $335 million of annual cost savings by 1999. She said the company was not setting a new target however.

In discussing results from the fourth quarter of 1996, Carr said credit card charge-offs rose to 5.23 percent from 4.67 percent in the third quarter. She said the charge-off ratio could continue rising in early 1997 but would then recede. She said credit cards continue to be a "good and profitable business."
